title: Director of Product Management

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: This role owns the complete product solution strategy for Epson's Professional Imaging division. Given that Epson's value proposition centers on enabling durable outdoor graphics but they don't control the protective film layer, this leader would care deeply about completing their solution stack. Tedlar partnership would address critical gaps: (1) COMPETITIVE DIFFERENTIATION - being able to offer validated 'print + protect' solutions with 20+ year durability claims versus HP/Canon/Mimaki competitors who also lack integrated protection solutions; (2) CUSTOMER SUCCESS METRICS - their print service provider customers face warranty claims and callbacks when graphics fail prematurely, which reflects poorly on Epson equipment performance and drives churn; (3) SOLUTION COMPLETENESS - currently customers must navigate fragmented overlaminate options themselves, creating friction in the sales cycle that a recommended Tedlar partnership would eliminate; (4) CREDIBILITY FOR OUTDOOR CLAIMS - Epson heavily markets 'weather-resistant' and 'outdoor durability' but actual longevity depends on overlaminates they don't control—Tedlar's 60+ year proven performance provides third-party validation of their outdoor messaging. This role controls product positioning, go-to-market strategy, and ecosystem partnerships, making them the primary decision-maker for strategic co-marketing relationships. They own P&L impact from customer retention and competitive win rates that Tedlar partnership would directly improve.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: Jason owns product strategy and solution positioning for Epson's Professional Imaging portfolio (SureColor S-Series solvent, R-Series resin, V-Series UV printers). He defines the complete customer value proposition, determines ecosystem partnerships (similar to existing relationships with ONYX Graphics RIP software and Graphtec cutters), and shapes go-to-market strategy. He likely reports to VP/GM of Professional Imaging division and manages Group Product Managers (like Matt McCausland). His decisions directly impact competitive positioning against HP, Canon, Mimaki, and Roland in the large-format printer market. He influences channel enablement strategy, co-marketing partnerships, and technical validation programs that resellers use to sell complete solutions.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: Jason would care specifically about Tedlar as an integrated solution component for Epson's outdoor graphics applications: (1) VEHICLE WRAPS - Epson's S-Series solvent printers are marketed for fleet graphics and wraps; Tedlar's graffiti resistance and UV protection would complete this solution for municipal fleets and commercial vehicles requiring long-term protection; (2) OUTDOOR SIGNAGE - Epson's V7000 UV flatbed (number one selling UV flatbed in North America) produces rigid outdoor signs where Tedlar overlaminate would extend lifespan and justify premium pricing for Epson equipment; (3) ARCHITECTURAL PANELS - Epson's large-format capability serves building facade applications where Tedlar's extreme weather resistance and temperature range performance would differentiate their output quality; (4) VALIDATED COMPLETE SYSTEM - Technical certification that Tedlar films are compatible with Epson's UltraChrome inks and PrecisionCore printheads would give resellers confidence to recommend the complete stack without trial-and-error.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: Jason is measured on product line revenue growth, competitive win rates versus HP/Canon/Mimaki, customer retention rates, and product margin performance. His personal pain points include: (1) Incomplete solution gaps that slow reseller sales cycles when customers ask 'what protective film should I use?'; (2) Customer churn when prints fail prematurely due to poor overlaminate choices, which damages Epson equipment reputation even though the printer performed correctly; (3) Competitive vulnerability when HP or Canon offer more complete turnkey solutions; (4) Difficulty substantiating Epson's 'outdoor durability' marketing claims without controlling the protective layer that actually determines longevity. Tedlar partnership directly addresses all four pain points by providing a validated, premium-tier protective solution he can integrate into product positioning and reseller enablement programs.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: IMMEDIATE TIMING OPPORTUNITY: Epson is exhibiting at ISA Sign Expo 2025 (April 23-25, Las Vegas, booth #2216) within the next month. Jason's team just launched the SureColor S9170 11-color solvent printer at this show, positioning it for premium outdoor applications. This creates perfect timing to discuss Tedlar partnership for the next product cycle and potentially coordinate presence at PRINTING United 2025 later this year. Additionally, Epson's active product refresh cycle (V1070, F9570H, R5070 all launched 2024) indicates they're in planning mode for 2026 product positioning and go-to-market strategy, making NOW the right time to integrate Tedlar into their solution stack before competitive positioning is locked.

personalization_hooks.hook: Epson markets weather-resistant outdoor durability but doesn't control the protective film layer that actually determines graphic longevity in the field
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Open by acknowledging the gap between Epson's premium equipment capabilities and the fragmented overlaminate landscape their customers navigate. Frame Tedlar as the missing piece that validates Epson's outdoor performance claims with proven track record, positioning this as solution completeness rather than material supply.

personalization_hooks.hook: Epson competes against HP, Canon, and Mimaki who also lack integrated protective film solutions, creating differentiation opportunity
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Position Tedlar partnership as competitive advantage Jason can own—being first to offer validated 'print + protect' system would differentiate Epson's solution selling versus competitors still selling equipment only. Reference how Epson already does this successfully with ONYX RIP software and Graphtec cutters.

personalization_hooks.hook: Epson's authorized reseller network needs complete workflow recommendations to accelerate sales cycles and reduce support burden
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Frame this as reseller enablement opportunity rather than product sale. Emphasize that Jason's product strategy decisions directly impact how easily resellers can sell and support Epson systems. Suggest starting with technical validation that Tedlar works optimally with UltraChrome inks, then building into reseller training and co-marketing programs.

recommended_approach: Lead with solution completeness and competitive differentiation angle. Position outreach as strategic partnership discussion rather than vendor pitch. Reference Epson's existing ecosystem partnerships (ONYX, Graphtec) to establish precedent. Suggest low-commitment starting point: technical validation that Tedlar films perform optimally with Epson's ink chemistries and printheads, which gives Jason tangible value even before broader partnership discussions. Acknowledge upcoming ISA Sign Expo as relevant context but don't push for meeting there—instead suggest post-show debrief as natural next step.
